Services: - Revenue from services is recognized as the performance obligations are satisfied. - If CDW acts as a principal, revenue is recognized when or as the customer obtains control of the service. - If acting as an agent, revenue is recognized when CDW arranges for a third party to provide the service, which may be upon contract execution or invoicing. - Extended warranties sold separately from hardware are considered distinct service performance obligations, and revenue is recognized accordingly as these services are provided. query: Impact of Church & Dwight coupon reserve mthd on P&L & cash flow w/ redemp variances: CHD
final_answer: Church & Dwight establishes coupon reserves based on historical redemption rates and trends. These reserves are recorded as reductions to sales at the time the related sales occur, directly impacting the income statement (P&L) by lowering reported revenue and, consequently, net income (see Chunks 1, 2, 3). If actual coupon redemptions differ from the estimated rates used to set the reserves, the impact is as follows: - If actual redemptions are higher than estimated, the company will need to increase the coupon reserve, resulting in additional reductions to sales and a negative impact on the P&L in the period the adjustment is made. - If actual redemptions are lower than estimated, the company will release part of the reserve, increasing reported sales and positively impacting the P&L in the adjustment period. The sensitivity of the reserve to changes in redemption rates is quantified: if the coupon redemption rate deviates by 0.1% from the rate for which reserves are accrued, it would result in a difference of approximately $0.7 million in the required reserve (Chunks 2, 3). Regarding cash flow, the coupon reserve is a non-cash accrual at the time of sale. Cash outflows occur when coupons are actually redeemed and paid. Variances between estimated and actual redemptions primarily affect the timing of cash outflows: - If redemptions are higher, actual cash outflows will be higher than originally expected. - If redemptions are lower, actual cash outflows will be lower. However, since the reserve is estimated and adjusted through accruals, immediate cash flow is not directly affected when the reserve is adjusted; the actual impact is seen when coupons are redeemed. Thus, changes in redemption rates primarily affect the P&L through adjustments to reserves, while cash flow is affected as coupons are actually redeemed and paid out. In summary: The coupon reserve method impacts the P&L by adjusting reported revenue based on estimated coupon redemptions. Variances from these estimates result in future adjustments to sales and net income. Cash flow is only affected when coupons are actually redeemed, not when reserves are adjusted.
